result: In 57 previously hospitalised COVID-19 patients vs 57 matched healthy controls (NAPKON-HAP), cortical thickness was reduced in parahippocampal gyri and temporal lobe, correlating with acute severity and Fatigue Severity Scale scores.
reason: Reports cortical thickness, not thalamus/basal ganglia/choroid plexus; controls are healthy not recovered; the grey-matter fit is covered by the separate neuro-mri-structure link.

result: In 57 previously hospitalised COVID-19 patients vs 57 matched healthy controls, cortical thickness was reduced in parahippocampal gyri and temporal lobe (FDR-significant), correlating with acute disease severity and long-term fatigue.
reason: Same structural grey-matter measure in a post-COVID population, adding to the post-infection grey-matter contrast; small, hospitalised (severity-confounded) sample, not ME/CFS.

result: CE-MS urinary peptidomics in 50 PASC vs 50 controls (42 healthy, 8 ME/CFS) found 195 differing peptides, mostly collagen alpha-chain fragments, consistent with altered collagen turnover; classifier AUC 0.949 training, 0.962 validation.
reason: Collagen degradation fragments in a long COVID version (urine rather than plasma); direction of change not stated and ME/CFS sat in the control group, so support is weak.

result: An SVM classifier from 195 urinary peptides (PASC195) separated 50 PASC patients from 50 controls with AUC 0.949 in derivation (n=60) and 0.962 in a held-out validation set (n=40).
reason: Long COVID single-omic classifier with only a within-study split validation, the high-internal-AUC situation the finding warns about; it does not test an external cohort, so it does not contradict.

result: In 55 post-COVID condition patients vs 36 COVID-recovered controls, ASL showed no significant regional CBF group difference after FDR correction; only at an exploratory threshold was fatigue associated with lower right occipital perfusion, and there was no cortical atrophy.
reason: Same resting ASL measure but the primary group comparison was null after correction, so not a replication; long COVID population, small sample, exploratory fatigue association only.

result: In the CONVALESCENCE study (306 community participants enrolled about 2 years post-infection, 12 months of smartwatch/app monitoring), long COVID cases with fatigue-cluster symptoms (n=50) had small persistent deficits across activity, exercise, cardiorespiratory, autonomic, sleep, cognitive and mental-health measures vs 152 controls, with no recovery over 12 months; long COVID without fatigue cluster (n=76) did not differ from controls.
reason: Adds objective time-course evidence that a fatigue-defined post-COVID subgroup stays impaired while others resemble controls, parallel to the Charité persistence finding; preprint, not ME/CFS criteria.

result: Fatigue-cluster long COVID cases showed small persistent deficits across systems, including smartwatch-derived autonomic function, vs controls over 12 months.
reason: Abstract gives no resting HR or HF-HRV results, only an undefined autonomic domain, and the population is long COVID not ME/CFS; too thin to link.

result: Meta-analysis of post-infective fatigue syndromes including long COVID (30 studies included, 11 meta-analysed, 413 cases) vs recovered controls from the same infection found higher white cell counts at 3-6 months (d=0.41) and higher RANTES (d=0.45) and TNF-alpha (d=0.30) at 6-12 months.
reason: Same circulating-cytokine measure with TNF effect similar to the CFS meta-analysis (0.30 vs 0.27), but in a post-infective/long COVID population with exposure-matched controls, so it extends rather than replicates.

result: Post-infective fatigue cases had higher WBC (d=0.41), RANTES (d=0.45) and TNF-alpha (d=0.30) than recovered controls in meta-analysis.
reason: Finding is about T-cell exhaustion, myeloid shifts, EBV antibodies and cortisol, none of which the paper reports; the cytokine fit is covered by the immune-cytokine-meta link.

result: In the Luxembourg CON-VINCE cohort (risk analysis n=1,865), female gender, lower resilience, loneliness and more comorbidities were associated with persistent symptoms; memory impairment with fatigue clustered only in post COVID (n=50), whereas depression with anxiety occurred in both infected and uninfected mimics (n=66).
reason: Independent cohort finding female sex as a risk factor for persistent post-COVID symptoms, same direction as RECOVER; no effect size given and the memory/fatigue cluster result is outside this finding.
